title: Bahrain says Iranian strike set industrial site ablaze; two tankers hit in Hormuz
dek: Shrapnel from intercepted missiles injured two people, Bahrain said. Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they hit US Patriot radars at two bases, a claim that could not be verified.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Bahrain said an Iranian missile and drone attack on Saturday evening set fire to a civilian industrial facility, and on Sunday said shrapnel from intercepted missiles had injured two people, one of them a Pakistani resident in critical condition. Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they had struck US military positions in the kingdom. On the same day two tankers were hit in the Strait of Hormuz.

"As a result of the heinous Iranian aggression, a civilian industrial facility was targeted, causing a fire at the site," Bahrain's interior ministry said on Saturday. It did not name the facility or say where it was, and said its first reports showed material damage but no injuries. Two residents said they saw smoke rising over Sitra Island on Bahrain's east coast, which hosts several industrial plants, including a refinery run by the state oil company Bapco, according to reports.

## What each side says

In its update on Sunday, the interior ministry said two people had been hurt by shrapnel from intercepted Iranian missiles: a Bahraini citizen with disabilities and a Pakistani resident, who it said was in a critical condition. It accused Tehran of a "systematic hostile approach" towards the kingdom. The Bahrain Defence Force said its air defences had dealt with "a number of treacherous Iranian aerial attacks" on Saturday and that falling debris had caused minor damage.

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) gave a different account. It said a combined missile and drone operation had targeted US military positions at the al-Riffa and Awali bases and hit two radars of US Army Patriot air-defence systems, according to reports. An Iranian news agency named different bases, and the claims could not be independently verified. The Guards warned that any violation of Iranian airspace would meet a "harsh and decisive response". Iranian state television said on Saturday that Iran had shot down a US drone over Qeshm Island. There was no immediate US comment on either claim.

Saudi Arabia's foreign ministry condemned the attack on the industrial site as a violation of international law and the UN Charter, expressed "full solidarity with Manama" and held Iran responsible, according to reports.

## Tankers hit in the strait

The UK Maritime Trade Operations centre (UKMTO), which monitors shipping in the region, said one tanker had been struck by an "unknown projectile" while passing through the Strait of Hormuz and that "there are no reported casualties at this time". A second tanker was reported to have been hit in its engine room.

Iran's army said a ship had caught fire after entering a "restricted zone" and hitting a mine, and that the tanker had switched off its identification and navigation systems "in defiance of issued warnings and maritime transit regulations", according to reports. The US military said recently that it had cleared mines from the main shipping routes through the strait.

## Background

The war began with US and Israeli strikes on Iran in February. The United States maintains a blockade of Iranian ports and escorts ships through Hormuz, and announced what it called an "economic asphyxiation" campaign against Iran in August. Bahrain, which hosts the US Navy's Fifth Fleet, has now been attacked several times in November: on 17 November US jets struck an IRGC missile site on Qeshm after Iranian drones were launched at Sheikh Isa Air Base.

Diplomacy is moving in parallel. A Qatari delegation held two hours of talks in Tehran on Friday, Iran's deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi said, without giving details. He called the US blockade "an act of war". Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said the talks in the region "must be given a chance", but that Iran's demands, including an end to the war on all fronts, the release of frozen assets and the lifting of oil sanctions and the blockade, had to be met.

## Why it matters for India

Much of India's imported crude oil and gas passes through Hormuz. On 16 November an attack on the LPG tanker MT Tara Gas left one Indian sailor missing and two injured; the Ministry of External Affairs said then that "the targeting of commercial shipping and civilian infrastructure must end". Bahrain is also home to a large Indian community. There was no statement from New Delhi on the latest attacks by Sunday evening.
